subject: Post-demo: Prompt collection & model fit follow-up
messages:
From: Ella Liu <ella@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Prompt collection & model fit follow-up

Thanks again for the demo this morning — really helpful walkthrough. A couple of follow-ups from our side as we start to scope an eval and pilot: 

1) Model recommendation: based on what you showed, which Redwood model variants would you suggest we start benchmarking for our customer-facing summarization flow (short financial reports, ~150-400 tokens)?

2) Prompt/edge-case collection: can you share a template we should use to collect customer prompts and edge cases? We have a set of ~200 prompts already but they include PII and some proprietary phrasing — want to make sure we send things in the right way.

3) Quality/regression concerns: any guidance on what baseline outputs we should provide (gold labels, heuristics) so Redwood can run automatic regression checks?

I'll attach a small sample of prompts to this thread. Happy to hop on a call if it's easier.

Thanks,
Ella
Senior Data Scientist | FinLytics
ella@finlytics.com

Attachment: sample_prompts.csv (stub - 12 rows)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ella Liu <ella@finlytics.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-07T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Prompt collection & model fit follow-up

Hey Ella — great to meet you earlier, and thanks for the clear asks. High level answers + next steps below.

Recommended starting models:
- redwood-7b-q4f (good latency / token cost; strong base summarization for shorter reports)
- redwood-13b-int8 (higher quality at ~2x latency, recommend for fidelity-sensitive flows)
- If you need the highest factuality for complex tables, we can run a quick A/B vs a tuned 13B variant we use for tabular summarization.

Prompt collection template: attached (prompt_set_template.csv). Please fill the columns: prompt_id, input_text, expected_output (if available), edge_case_flag (yes/no), contains_pii (yes/no), pii_type (if applicable), notes. We typically ask for the top ~50 production prompts plus 20-30 edge cases to start.

Quality / regression guidance:
- If you can provide gold outputs for ~200 prompts that'd be ideal for initial scoring (metrics we use: normalized ROUGE-L, exact-match on key entities, and a small set of human-judged quality scores).
- If gold labels aren't available, provide a set of acceptance heuristics (e.g., "must include company name and 3 key bullets") and a small reference set for manual review.

Security/redaction: please do not send raw PII. If prompts contain names/accounts, replace with placeholders per the template (e.g., [PERSON_NAME], [ACCOUNT_ID]). We can also support client-side redaction for Private deployments — will loop in details below.

Links: benchmark run (high-level): https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmarks/20260303/finlytics-run
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/FIN-2026-8421

Next steps:
- Please upload the completed prompt_set_template.csv and the ~20 edge cases to the Drive folder (link below) or send via your secure S3 link.
- Dylan/Ava from our ML team will propose an initial eval plan once we have the sample prompts and desired acceptance criteria.
- Suggest 30-min sync to align scope — are you available Wed 3/10 at 10am PT?

Attaching: prompt_set_template.csv; attaching a PDF summary of the demo benchmarks: redwood_benchmark_run_20260303.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redaction-guidelines

Quick lane from ML: thanks for including us. A couple of practical asks to speed up a meaningful eval: 

- Acceptance criteria: please tell us which metrics matter most to you (factuality/precision on key entities, semantic similarity thresholds, or stylistic constraints). We'll map them to automated signals plus a small human eval.
- Baseline outputs: ideally we get (a) gold labels for 100-200 prompts, or (b) expected-output heuristics for scoring. If neither is possible, even a small set of "anchor" prompts with reference outputs helps calibrate thresholds.
- Regression monitoring: we'll set up a prompt-set-based test harness (runs nightly for Dedicated/Private customers). To flag regressions we need a baseline model version + the test set. If you can share which model(s) you consider baseline, we'll compute delta metrics and set alert thresholds.

If you prefer, we can draft a one-page eval plan after we see the sample prompts — will hold on that until we get the spreadsheet.

Thanks,
Dylan
Applied ML | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa/Dylan — appreciate the detail. I've attached a small export (sample_prompts.csv) and included a couple of notes inline below.

Sample prompt excerpts: 
- prompt_id: P-001 | input_text: "Summarize the attached Q1 report for Acme Holdings focusing on revenue drivers." | contains_pii: yes | pii_type: ORGANIZATION
- prompt_id: P-007 | input_text: "Redact any client names and summarize the client feedback for account 3829." | contains_pii: yes | pii_type: ACCOUNT_ID
- prompt_id: P-012 | input_text: "Produce a one-paragraph executive summary and three bullets with risk items." | contains_pii: no

Edge cases we flagged: nested tables, mixed language inputs (EN + ES), prompts with bullet lists that include numeric financial ratios.

PII question: some of our prompts include small snippets of customer-identifying info. What's the minimum redaction you need to run the eval? Do you support wildcarding or token masking so we can send fewer sanitized samples initially? Also please confirm whether your hosted API will log prompts unredacted (we're evaluating Private for this reason).

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Prompt collection & model fit follow-up

Thanks Ella — this is perfect. Quick answers and proposed next steps: 

Redaction guidance (short):
- Replace direct identifiers with placeholders: [PERSON_NAME], [ORG_NAME], [ACCOUNT_ID]. Do not use real values in the spreadsheet.
- For numeric identifiers where format matters (account numbers), replace digits with Xs of the same length (e.g., 3829 -> XXXX) so parsing features still behave correctly.
- For table excerpts, remove entire rows that contain sensitive balances and replace with a summarized row (e.g., "TABLE_REDACTED_SUMMARY").

Hosted vs Private: our hosted API does persist logs for usage and troubleshooting; for evals we recommend either (a) upload a redacted prompt set to our secure Drive/S3 and run the eval on Hosted with redacted data, or (b) if you need no logs/retention, we can run the eval on a Private deployment or run client-side redaction + ephemeral keys. We'll include a short doc on client-side redaction best practices in the Drive folder.

Eval plan + thresholds: Dylan/Ava will draft a 1-page eval plan after they ingest the sample_prompts.csv and any gold outputs you can provide. We'll run redwood-7b-q4f and redwood-13b-int8 by default and report ROUGE-L, exact-match on named entities, and a small human quality score (1-5).

Next steps:
- Please re-upload a redacted version of the prompt_set_template.csv to this Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redaction-guidelines (or send via your secure S3 link).
- Dylan will follow up with a draft eval plan within 48 hours of receiving the redacted spreadsheet.
- Confirm 30-min sync: Wed 2026-03-10 at 10:00 AM PT works for us — I'll send a calendar invite unless you prefer a different time.

I'll attach the redaction checklist and the prompt template to make it easy.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
